title: Resolved experiment
description: Canonical resolved-experiment.json: the single machine-readable intent a benchctl attempt executes, resolved from a scenario TOML plus profile, cluster profile, subjects file, adapter describe documents, and seed. Authored by crates/benchctl (resolve.rs) and consumed by every adapter through `<adapter> validate|run --experiment`. Documentation mirror of the ResolvedExperiment serde type in crates/bench-schema/src/experiment.rs, which is the source of truth.

name.description: Scenario name carried from the source TOML.

kind.description: Only the producer experiment kind exists in milestone 0.

profile.description: Resolution profile applied on top of the scenario, for example a smoke or headline profile.

claim_eligible.description: Always false in milestone 0; claim eligibility requires calibrated runner classification.

load_mode.description: Resolved load model. Source TOMLs carry the longer legacy strings (closed-loop-capacity-point, scheduled-open-loop-capacity-search); the resolver normalizes them to these two.

records.description: Measured record count. Identity-relevant numbers are integers only.

offered_records_per_second.description: Required if and only if load_mode is scheduled-open-loop-fixed-rate, enforced by ResolvedExperiment::validate().

arrival.description: Arrival process the scheduled load mode draws its intended offsets from. Required if and only if load_mode is scheduled-open-loop-fixed-rate, and absent otherwise. Only deterministic has an implementation in this milestone; an adapter handed poisson declines it in its validate report rather than silently substituting the schedule it does implement.

seed.description: Deterministic seed for payload generation and execution-order selection. Part of the experiment identity.

application.description: ApplicationSpec: how the benchmark application offers records - instance count, concurrency, and the shape of the admission and completion surfaces it uses. The application-boundary budgets live here, not under `budget`: they bound what the client is allowed to hold, which is part of the workload, whereas `budget` bounds how long the control plane will wait.

backpressure.description: What the application does when admission is refused, as a vocabulary the adapter interprets - for example block-within-original-offer.

queue_bytes.description: Bytes the client may hold in its own queues.

max_outstanding_records.description: Records the application allows to be outstanding at once.

payload.description: PayloadSpec: record body shape and its deterministic generator. There is no per-payload seed and no keyed flag - the experiment's single top-level `seed` drives every deterministic choice, and keyed records are a deferred workload row (see scenarios/DEFERRED.md).

bytes.description: Payload size in bytes, identical for every record.

identity.description: Human description of the self-check envelope, when the profile has one - for example 'KFB1 plus 16-byte run ID plus 64-bit sequence'. Absent when the profile has no envelope.

producer.description: ProducerSpec: normalized durability, batching, and retry settings every subject must honor.

warmup_partitioning.description: Partition assignment for the warmup phase, when it differs from the measured phase. Absent when it does not.

warmup_serialized_partition_primer_recor.description: Records the warmup sends serially to prime every partition leader, so the measured phase does not pay for metadata discovery. Absent when the warmup does no priming.

budget.description: BudgetSpec: the ceilings the attempt declares for itself. These are part of the intent rather than an operational detail - a run that needed twice the wall clock to finish did not measure the same thing - so they are hashed into the experiment id along with everything else. Application-boundary queue and outstanding-record bounds are NOT here; they live under `application`.

run_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one subject may run before the control plane kills it.

tool_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds a configured tool - topic creation, verification - may run.

probe_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds an adapter probe (describe, validate) may run.

max_captured_output_bytes.description: Bytes of a probe's output the control plane will read before giving up.

cluster.description: ClusterSpec: required broker topology and topic durability, independent of any bootstrap address.

slo.description: SloSpec: predeclared service-level objectives used to classify a run as sustainable.

subjects.description: Subjects under comparison, in declaration order. Each subject's command is excluded from the experiment identity so that rebuilding a binary elsewhere does not change the identity.

name.description: Subject identity, also used to derive topic names; charset-validated at resolve time.

command.description: Adapter argv prefix. Excluded from the experiment identity.

role.description: What this subject is for: the denominator of the comparison, the subject under test, or the anchor held fixed across attempts. Absent means unlabeled. Unlike command, role is included in the experiment identity when present - two experiments that disagree about which subject is the baseline are asking different questions - and omitting it entirely leaves every pre-role identity unchanged.

runtime.description: RuntimeBinding: the concrete cluster and naming this attempt used. Excluded from the experiment identity, so the same intent keeps one identity across attempts and clusters. Omitted entirely - not null - in the output of a bare `resolve`, which describes intent that has not been run yet.

run_id.description: First 16 hex characters of sha256(experiment_id || attempt_id).

topics.description: Per-subject measured and warmup topics, keyed by subject name.

execution_order.description: Subject names in the order they were executed.
